'''Yoda's Hut''' or '''Yoda's house''' was both the home and final resting place of [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].

==Description==
[[File:ITW_Yoda_hut.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Yoda's hut was worked into a gnarltree.]]
Yoda's Hut,<ref name="DB">{{DB|location|yodashut|Yoda's Hut}}</ref> also known as Yoda's house,<ref name="CL">''[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|Star Wars: Complete Locations]]''</ref> was a simple,<ref name="DB" /> sturdy,<ref name="FF46">{{FactFile|46|DAG 7-8|Dagobah – Yoda's Hut}}</ref> hand-built<ref name="CL" /> hut<ref name="DB" /> worked into the roots of an old, immense,<ref name="FF46" /> fearsome-looking<ref name="DB" /> [[Gnarltree/Legends|gnarltree]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]]. The home was located atop a [[Moss/Legends|moss]]-covered knoll at the edge of a<ref name="CL" /> deep<ref name="FF46" /> sweet [[Water/Legends|water]] lagoon<ref name="CL" /> that never flooded.<ref name="FF46" /> The hut, which was small in size, was constructed<ref name="FF46" /> using the wattle-and-daub building method<ref name="CL" /> with mud, [[Stone/Legends|stones]], [[Tree/Legends|tree]] limbs, and cut vine. The house featured a curved, flowing design that went along with the natural order of the swamp.<ref name="FF46" /> Leaves, roots and vines covered the exterior of the hut and local twigs and grasses reinforced the home's plaster.<ref name="CL" />

[[File:YodaHut-hd.png|thumb|left|300px|The interior of Yoda's hut.]]
Yoda's house was comprised of three parts: a sitting room, a kitchen, and a small sleeping loft. The sturdy and waterproof foundation of the home was made from spacecraft deck-plating, and the floor was covered with low-fire clay tiles grouted with mortar. The house had skylights<ref name="CL" /> and small windows that almost appeared like balefully glowing [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] gazing out into darkness. This was caused by the heavy upper lid that kept the near-constant rain of Dagobah out of the house.<ref name="FF46" /> The windowpanes were possibly made from precious gems or from [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] viewports of an abandoned vessel.<ref name="CL" /> The sitting area was accessed by a small entrance<ref name="FF46" /> that incorporated the nozzle system of a spacecraft from the era of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="CL" />  The entrance tunnel sloped down to the swamps and prevented water from getting into the house.<ref name="FF46" />

==History==
[[File:Yoda_hut.jpg|thumb|left|150px|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda's]] hut, [[9 ABY/Legends|five years after his death]].]]
Yoda used the remains of his decayed [[E3-standard starship lifeboat/Legends|escape pod]] to construct his hut.<ref name="db2" />

Though he was largely undisturbed in his humble abode, there were rare cases in which Yoda's privacy was intruded upon.

A [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of [[Galen Marek]], [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], met Yoda when he visited Dagobah to [[Cave of Evil/Legends|find himself]].<ref name="TFU II">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

[[File:Yodahut_ST.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Yoda and Luke Skywalker inside his hut.]]
[[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] landed on Dagobah to find Yoda and complete his [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]] at the behest of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]]. After landing in the swamp, Skywalker met the Jedi Master, who took him back to his hut.<ref name="SWE5" /> Skywalker later had to find his way back to the hut as part of his training.<ref name="Rebel Strike III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> He would return sometime later to complete his training, but found Yoda to be nearing the end of his life, and remained at his Master and friend's bedside as the last of the Jedi entrusted his kind's future to Luke and peacefully passed on to the afterlife.<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}''</ref> After Yoda's death, his hut was abandoned and decayed over time. Luke Skywalker visited the remains of Yoda's hut<ref name="HTTE">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]]<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> as did [[Ikrit]]<ref name="Anakin's Quest">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: Anakin's Quest]]''</ref> in [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]].<ref name="TERC" />

[[Arhul Hextrophon/Legends|Arhul Hextrophon]] met Yoda here, although the scholar kept it to himself.<ref name="SWS">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:RMQ-YodasHut.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]].]]
Originally Yoda's hut was to resemble a mosque with stained glass windows, though this concept was abandoned to illustrate the Jedi's minimalist outlook. It was probably also deserted for purely practical reasons. Because of the combination of the hut's small quarters and the puppeteers operating Yoda, any action in the hut required the moves to be carefully plotted beforehand to allow for good camera angles. It had walls thick enough that insects took a long time to make their way in.

In the [[2001]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', Yoda's Hut, along with Yoda, Skywalker, and R2-D2, appeared as an [[Easter egg (virtual)|easter egg]] in the third level of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] campaign; "[[Raid on Spearhead]]." The hut can be seen if the player uses a cheat code to explore the inaccessible areas of the map, and can also be placed in player-made levels in the scenario editor.<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>
